title: A Microfluidic Platform for High-throughput Single-cell Isolation and Culture
protocol: Use 4-inch silicon wafers as a substrate.
Dehydrate the wafers in a conventional oven at 120°C for 10 minutes.
Clean the dehydrated silicon wafers using oxygen plasma treatment at 100 watts for 30 seconds.
Preheat two hotplates at 65°C and 95°C, respectively.
Coat 5 g of negative photoresist on the cleaned silicon wafers by spinning at 1200 rpm for 30 seconds.
Place the coated wafer on a preheated hotplate at 65°C for 12 minutes.
Transfer the wafer to another preheated hotplate at 95°C for 33 minutes.
Align the PR-coated silicon wafer to a 25,400 dpi resolution transparency photomask.
Expose the photoresist coated silicon wafer to UV light (365 nm) with a dose of 500 mJ/cm².
Place the exposed wafer on a hotplate for post-baking at 95°C for 12 minutes.
Soak the wafers in SU-8 developer solution for 12 min.
Gently dry the wafers with nitrogen gas.
Coat 5 g of negative photoresist on the wafers using a spin coater at 700 rpm for 30 sec and then at 1,200 rpm for 30 sec for pattern thicknesses of 300 µm and 27 µm respectively.
Place the PR coated wafer on a hotplate at 65 °C for 4 min followed by 95 °C for 8 min (for 27 µm thick pattern).
Place the PR coated silicon wafer on the mask aligner equipped with UV light and expose to 365 nm UV light at a dose of 250 mJ/cm².
Bake the wafers at 95 °C for 5 min (for 27 µm thick pattern).
Wash off uncrosslinked photoresist by soaking in PGMEA solution for 6 min (for 27 µm thick pattern) and dry with nitrogen gas.
Measure the height of pattern features on the wafer using a scanning laser profilometer.
Switch the observation mode from "camera view" to "laser view".
Set the upper and lower positions of the features.
Set the measurement mode, area, quality, and z-pitch up to transparent (top), 1 line (1,024 x 1), high-accuracy and 0.5 µm, respectively.
Press the start button to begin the measurement.
Silanize the master molds with trichlorosilane to create a hydrophobic surface.
Place the master molds and a weighting boat containing 200 μl of trichlorosilane in a desiccator.
Apply vacuum (-85 kPa) for 15 min.
Leave the master molds in the desiccator at room temperature for at least 1 hr to silanize the master molds.
Remove the master molds from the desiccator and place each master mold in a 10 cm Petri dish.
Mix a total amount of 17.6 g PDMS polymer kit containing a base and a curing agent at a ratio of 10:1.
Pour the PDMS onto the silanized master mold in the Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish in a desiccator and apply vacuum (-85 kPa) for 1 hr to remove air bubbles in the PDMS.
Remove the Petri dish from the desiccator and place it in a conventional oven at 65 °C for 3 - 6 hr to cure the PDMS.
Remove cured PDMS replicas from master molds.
Punch two holes as an inlet and outlet at the ends of the microchannel on the capture-well array PDMS replica using a puncher with an inner diameter of 0.75 mm for the fluidic channel.
Clean the surface of the PDMS replicas with tape.
Place the PDMS replicas in a plasma cleaner for oxygen plasma treatment (100 watts for 14 seconds).
Remove the PDMS replicas from the oxygen plasma machine.
Align a top and bottom PDMS replica by hand under a stereomicroscope.
Bring the aligned PDMS replicas into contact.
Place the aligned PDMS replicas in an oven at 65 °C for 24 hours to achieve permanent bonding between the PDMS replicas.
Soak the PDMS device in deionized (DI)-water filled container and place the container under vacuum (-85 kPa) for 15 minutes to remove air from the microchannel of the PDMS device.
Place the DI water-filled PDMS device in a tissue culture hood.
Sterilize the device with UV light (wavelength: 254 nm) for 30 minutes.
Replace the DI water in the PDMS device with a 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 1x PBS solution and incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes to prevent cells from sticking to the PDMS surface.
Replace the 5% BSA solution in the PDMS device with sterilized 1x PBS.
Prepare cells from neural stem cell KT98, human carcinoma cell A549, and MDA-MB-435 in a Petri dish under conventional cell culture conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity).
Remove spent DMEM basal medium with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% antibiotics from the culture dish when cells reach 70 - 80% confluence.
Gently wash the cells three times with sterilized PBS.
Discard the PBS after washing.
Add 2 ml of a recombinant enzyme mixture to disperse the cells at room temperature for 5 min.
Tap the culture dish gently to facilitate cell detachment.
Add 4 ml of sterilized PBS to disperse cells and transfer the suspension to a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of sterilized PBS.
Count live cells using the Trypan Blue exclusion method.
Load 50 µl of cell suspension at a concentration of 2.2 - 2.5 x106 cells/ml into the microchannel of the PDMS device via the outlet hole with a handheld pipette.
Hold the pipette at the first stop position to avoid introducing air bubbles.
Load another 50 µl of cell suspension through the inlet hole to evenly fill up the whole microchannel with cells.
Seal the outlet hole with a UV sterilized plug (a 3 mm long, 1 mm diameter cut nylon fishing line).
Fill up a 1 ml sterile syringe with culture medium and connect it to the inlet hole via a 23 G blunt needle and PTFE tubing.
Remove the plug from the outlet hole and allow a 2-min time interval for cells to settle into single-cell capture-wells by gravitational force.
Wash away uncaptured cells with 300 µl of culture medium at a flow rate of 600 µl/min driven by the syringe pump.
Wait for 2 min to stabilize the device, and seal both inlet and outlet holes with plugs to form a closed culture system.
Flip the device by hand to transfer captured single-cells to the culture microwells.
Place the PDMS device in a 100-mm tissue culture dish.
Add 10 ml of sterilized PBS around the device.
Move the culture dish to a conventional cell culture incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity).
After 1 day of culture, replace the culture medium in the PDMS device with fresh medium.
Place two droplets of culture medium on top of the PDMS device near the inlet and outlet holes areas.
Punch two holes from the top of the PDMS device near the two ends of the microchannel as an inlet and an outlet for the microchannel.
Connect a 1 ml plastic syringe containing fresh medium to the inlet via a 23 G blunt needle and PTFE tubing.
Flow 120 μl fresh medium into the device for 5 min to replace the old medium.
Insert two plugs to seal the inlet and outlet holes.
Return the device to the cell culture incubator.
Refresh the culture medium every 2 days during the period of culture by removing the sealing plugs.
Repeat steps of replacing the medium as previously described.
